summary: Concept-stage gate over PRD.md (653 lines, commit 808558c, branch build-brief-run2), reviewed against its own source brief at /Users/m5/Downloads/dev-harness-BUILD-BRIEF_2.md. Decision is GO. The three things a concept gate exists to judge are all real here: the done-state is stated as seven metrics with thresholds and a named measuring command, with M5's threshold left explicitly open rather than faked; the out-of-scope list carries nine items each with its reason; and the falsification pass in section 7 changed four requirements and accepted two as weak on the record instead of gesturing at risk. I did not take the document's evidence on trust. Six load-bearing claims were re-derived in this context from the tree directly and every one held: the three named guards are absent from bollard/; store.py reads MI 4.78 grade C, max_cc 32, SLOC 1443; store.py churn is 1 against a 9-commit tree, so hotspot_signal reduces to max_cc exactly as R18 states; atlas/ingest/audit.py writes payload_json verbatim with no scrub; git ls-files returns zero for all three measurement scripts; and an independent fourth search over /Users/m5/dev for layered_command_guard.py and its four class names returns only PRD.md itself. GO rather than HOLD on the R14/R15 provenance question, deliberately. That question is already quarantined correctly - the PRD forbids R14/R15 entering a backlog or being sized until the operator settles it - so it is a drawn scope boundary, not a leak. It is also unresolvable by any action the architecture stage could take, which makes a Hold on it an open-ended Hold of the kind this skill's section 6 forbids, and it would stall roughly eighteen requirements that do not depend on it. It travels forward as an operator question with a default attached, per condition C1. One finding of my own, not inherited: section 8 records R0 as 'Closed by Run 1', and that claim does not survive checking. DEVH-3 is status=open in TESSERA - closed in prose by a peer session, never transitioned on the ticket. On the evidence question, this package's first revision said no dev-harness-scoped run existed; that was wrong on the specifics and is corrected here. A scoped run was produced: /Users/m5/dev/investigation/dev-harness-token-bloat-diagnostic-scoped-20260901.txt, 297 bytes, hint='dev-harness'. Reading it makes section 8 more wrong, not less. It reports 1.16x against a 1.1x target - OVER target - while the brief closes R0 on a 0.96x 'at parity, under the 1.1x target' figure. Two dev-harness-scoped numbers, disagreeing, and neither has surviving raw output: 0.96x was never shown, and 1.16x's JSON was overwritten in place by a later /dev-wide run to the same fixed output path, leaving only the console summary. That overwrite is R23's own argument landing concretely - an untracked tool writing to a fixed path silently destroys the prior run's raw output - which moves R23 from hygiene to load-bearing. R0 remains genuinely unsettled across two framings, neither complete. None of this blocks the gate: R0 is out of this PRD's scope and no R1-R24 requirement rests on it. It does make section 8 wrong, and condition C2 requires the correction. This package was written by a session that did not author the PRD, did not author the brief, and holds none of the reasoning that produced either. Recorded explicitly because concept_gate.py's own docstring names the unenforceability of that separation as a known open limitation - the hook cannot check it, so the claim belongs on the record instead.
